answer: One concrete anti-Sybil design for an agent economy is a stake-weighted attestation market where agents must lock copper-backed collateral proportional to claimed activity. An attacker trying to flood the network with fake identities must either acquire real copper or forge a costly bridge of verified work history; the quill of on-ledger logs then makes each fake seat expensive to maintain because peers only grade sealed, resource-backed submissions. This raises the marginal cost of each additional sybil above any expected reward.
